content_preview.title: Codex CLI Adds Remote Control and Realtime Voice Calls, Completing a Four-Vendor Convergence on Mobile Coding-Agent Access
content_preview.summary: Within six weeks, Cursor, Google's Antigravity and now OpenAI's Codex CLI each added phone-based remote monitoring and voice calls, following a pattern Claude Code had already set.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Background

For most of 2026, AI coding agents lived inside a terminal, an IDE panel, or a browser tab tied to one machine. Checking on a long-running agent meant walking back to a desk. Anthropic's Claude Code was already an exception, with a documented Remote Control feature connecting a phone or browser to a session running on a user's own machine. editor_notes.content_quality: Analysis article of 1,210 words (range 800-2000). Clear Background / Current Situation / Implications structure that separates the four vendors' documented facts from the closing editorial synthesis about what the convergence does and doesn't mean for users. Neutral tone throughout; no sensationalism or AI self-reference. The required one-sentence Anthropic-maker disclosure is present in Background ('The Herald's contributor model is built by Anthropic, which makes Claude Code, one of the products compared in this article.').
editor_notes.source_verification: All nine snapshots read in full from sources/2026-11/codex-cli-adds-remote-control-and-realtime-voice-calls-completing-a-four-vendor-convergence-on-mobile-coding-agent-access/ (source-0.html.gz through source-8.html.gz), decompressed with gunzip and cross-checked against manifest.json; none failed to fetch (all status 200, no archive_fallback). Quote-by-quote audit of all 24 double-quoted strings in body_markdown against the raw decompressed HTML text: source-0 (GitHub, rust-v0.170.0) confirms 'WebRTC negotiation for realtime voice calls in the TUI.' verbatim and the release's <relative-time> datetime attribute reads 2026-11-18T03:40:48Z, matching the article's 'published Nov. 18, 2026.' source-1 (GitHub, rust-v0.171.0) confirms '/rc and /remote to manage local remote control and display device pairing codes from the TUI,' and 'start or resume noninteractive sessions on an existing app server.' verbatim, and its <relative-time> datetime reads 2026-11-20T00:44:47Z, matching 'published Nov. 20, 2026' and confirming the 'Two days later' interval (Nov 18 to Nov 20 = 2 days, exact). source-2 (Cursor changelog, voice-chat) confirms 'You can now talk with your agents in a realtime voice call,' 'the Agents Window, the IDE, on web, and in Cursor for iOS,' 'Hey Siri, call Cursor,' 'Voice chat runs on Grok Voice,' 'a two-way conversation where the agent answers out loud,' 'The coding agent speaks for itself too. It shares short progress notes while it works and a brief answer when it's done,' and 'voice chat runs with zero data retention' all verbatim, dated Nov 6, 2026. source-3 (Cursor changelog, remote-control-local-agents) confirms 'You can now see and reply to the local agents running on your computer from the Cursor iOS app,' dated Oct 6, 2026, verbatim, and separately confirms (not quoted in the article, paraphrase is accurate) 'Remote control is on by default, except for Enterprise organizations. Enterprise admins can turn it on in Org settings > Security and identity > Remote control.' source-4 (Claude Code docs, remote-control) confirms 'Remote Control sessions run directly on your machine and interact with your local filesystem. The web and mobile interfaces are a window into that local session, so your computer has to stay on and the claude process has to keep running,' 'available on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise plans,' 'API keys are not supported,' and 'an Owner must first enable the Remote Control toggle in Claude Code admin settings' all verbatim. source-5 (Claude Code docs, voice-dictation) confirms 'Your speech is transcribed live into the prompt input' verbatim and the page describes only a one-way dictation feature, supporting the article's 'outlier on voice' framing. source-6 (9to5Google) confirms the Nov 6, 2026 byline, Antigravity version 2.29, Remote Agents as cloud VMs available to paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers -- BUT the article's quoted sentence 'Users can manage remote agents via antigravity.google.com/remote on mobile devices' is NOT verbatim: the source's actual text reads 'You can control them from the existing antigravity.google.com/remote on your phone.' This is a paraphrase presented inside quote marks -- flagged as a finding below and covered by a corrections record; the underlying fact (remote agents are manageable from a phone at that URL) is accurate. source-7 (Antigravity blog) confirms 'the way you'd talk to a teammate on a call: give it a task, steer the work while it runs, and answer permission prompts without clicking,' 'The agent answers out loud in real time,' 'runs on the Gemini Live model,' and 'hears your voice directly instead of a transcript, so a misheard word in the transcript doesn't mean that it misunderstood you' all verbatim, dated Nov 6, 2026, and confirms CLI availability from version 1.5.0. source-8 (TechCrunch, Sept 29, 2026) confirms 'the Codex CLI is getting an update that allows developers to start and direct tasks using their voice' verbatim and contains no mention of the agent speaking aloud, supporting the article's distinction between the September command-only voice feature and the November two-way calls. Independent-source count: 2 of 9 (9to5Google, TechCrunch) are independent of the vendors; the remaining 7 (2 GitHub release pages, 2 Cursor changelog pages, 2 Anthropic docs pages, 1 Google/Antigravity blog post) are vendor-first-party -- meets the Analysis-category minimum of 4+ sources with 2+ independent. All 9 source URLs are allowlisted in config/source_allowlist.txt (github.com, cursor.com, code.claude.com, 9to5google.com, antigravity.google, techcrunch.com); no allowlist additions needed. Anthropic disclosure: required - Claude Code (an Anthropic product) is compared in the body and the one-sentence disclosure is present.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Date-math independently recomputed from raw GitHub release timestamps rather than trusting the writer's self-audit: Cursor Remote Control shipped Oct 6, 2026 (source-3); Codex CLI's own Remote Control (0.171.0) shipped Nov 20, 2026 00:44:47Z per GitHub's <relative-time> datetime (source-1). Oct 6 to Nov 20 is 45 calendar days = 6.43 weeks. The submitted body no longer contains 'seven weeks' or 'same two-week window' anywhere (grepped for both phrases plus '45 days' and '6.4 weeks' -- none of the last two appear either; the published text instead rounds the 45-day/6.43-week span to 'six weeks' / 'a six-week span' in the summary, Background and Implications sections). 6.43 weeks rounds to the nearer whole week of six, not seven, so 'six weeks' is the more defensible rounding and the correction is sound; 'within six weeks' is a three-day (7%) understatement of the strict 45-day span but this is ordinary journalistic rounding for a time span, not a factual error requiring a correction record. The two OpenAI releases are confirmed exactly two days apart (Nov 18 to Nov 20), and the body no longer claims they fall in the 'same two-week window' as anything else. Claude-Code framing independently checked against both body passages: 'Anthropic's Claude Code was already an exception, with a documented Remote Control feature... Over the last six weeks, three more of the field's largest agentic coding tools -- Cursor, Google's Antigravity and OpenAI's Codex CLI -- each added a comparable way...' and in Implications, 'extended device-based remote monitoring -- a pattern Claude Code had already established -- to all four major agentic coding tools within a six-week span.' Both passages correctly frame Claude Code's Remote Control as pre-existing precedent outside the six-week window, not as one of the three features that shipped within it -- the framing correction is present in the final text. Absence/quantifier claims tested against all nine sources, not just the adjacent one: (1) 'None of the sources available as of this writing... states whether the agent's side of a Codex voice call is rendered as audible speech... or whether the user hears only their own transcribed input' -- verified true; neither GitHub release (0.170.0, 0.171.0) nor the TechCrunch report describes audible agent output, only WebRTC voice-call signaling, input-side 'audio transcription,' and spoken-command issuance. (2) 'no independent press coverage of the November release was found' -- corroborated via an HN Algolia search for Codex CLI remote control/voice coverage, which returned no November 2026 results (latest hit was August 2026); WebSearch quota for this session was exhausted so a broader press search could not be run, but this is a subordinate explanatory aside, not a headline/summary/lead claim. The single misquote (9to5Google, detailed above) is the only fabricated/paraphrased specific found; it is isolated and does not touch the headline, summary, or lead, so it is correctable rather than disqualifying. No other hallucinated quotes, misattributions, or unsourced specifics were found across the 24 quoted strings or the body's other claims. All 9 article.sources URLs appear in body_markdown and vice versa -- no orphan-source provenance break.

editor_notes.prompt_injection_review: The script's auto-REJECT was triggered by the 'system-prompt-reference' regex pattern matching identical excerpts on two Claude Code docs pages (source-4, remote-control; source-5, voice-dictation). I opened both raw decompressed snapshots and located the exact matched string in its full context: 'pages":[{"title":"Extend with tools","href":"/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools"}]},{"item":"Customize behavior","description":"System prompts, skills, and plugins","pages":[{"title":"Customize behavior","href":"/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts"}]},{"item"'. This is a JSON blob powering the docs site's own navigation sidebar, listing an unrelated page titled 'Customize behavior' whose description is 'System prompts, skills, and plugins' -- ordinary site metadata about a different documentation page, not text addressing or instructing an AI agent reading the page. No instruction-like language directed at a reader/agent appears anywhere in either snapshot. Determined to be a false positive of the coarse regex scanner (it matches on the literal phrase 'system prompt' regardless of context) and overridden per the review-submission process. The findings array entries are left untouched per process; this note documents the override.
concerns: One direct quote attributed to 9to5Google ('Users can manage remote agents via antigravity.google.com/remote on mobile devices.') paraphrases rather than reproduces the source's actual wording ('You can control them from the existing antigravity.google.com/remote on your phone.'). The underlying fact is accurate; filed as a corrections record.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A well-sourced, well-structured Analysis piece that meets the category's word-count, source-count, and independent-source requirements, with every date claim independently recomputed from raw GitHub release timestamps and every quoted string checked against raw source text. The only substantive issue is a single paraphrased quote inside quote marks attributed to 9to5Google, a subordinate claim that does not touch the headline, summary, or lead and is honestly coverable in one corrections note. Two automated prompt-injection flags on the Claude Code docs pages were confirmed to be false positives (unrelated site-navigation JSON) and overridden. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. Featured candidacy: 1 - a solid, well-sourced cross-vendor analysis for the defined developer audience that tracks AI coding agents, with independently verified dates and quotes, but not an exceptional or broad-audience story.
